notices.title: Slabtown: shallow launch and day-use access
notices.text: The Forest Service lists the boating site as open. Day use is 6 a.m.–10 p.m.; gravel buildup can make the ramp very shallow and current can be swift. Scout the launch during your shuttle and follow posted conditions.

takeOutAccess.operator: USDA Forest Service — Mark Twain National Forest
takeOutAccess.sourceName: USDA Forest Service — current Slabtown boating-site inventory
takeOutAccess.note: The Forest Service IVM record identifies a separate BOATING SITE, site_cn 6200427010602, marked OPEN and updated November 4, 2026. Its coordinate matches the riverbank access below the picnic/camping area in imagery. The older closed EDW record describes dispersed camping at a different point. Current agency boating instructions support the public launch; exact shoreline and current ramp usability remain unconfirmed. Stable access ID retained. The nearby Paddy Creek closure covers FR211, camping and trails, not the Slabtown boating-site approach shown in the order map.
takeOutAccess.directions: From Licking, follow Highway 32 west to Highway N, then Highway AF to the signed Slabtown access. Follow the public entrance downhill to the launch at the road end. The Area marker identifies the boating facility, not a surveyed water edge; scout the landing during your shuttle. Day use: 6 a.m.–10 p.m. Gravel buildup makes the ramp shallow, and current can be swift.

putInAccess.operator: USDA Forest Service — Mark Twain National Forest
putInAccess.sourceName: USDA Forest Service, Mark Twain NF — EDW Recreation Opportunities record
putInAccess.note: Public river access is documented by USDA Forest Service, Mark Twain NF — EDW Recreation Opportunities record. The coordinate is USFS EDW Recreation Opportunities (Mark Twain National Forest), OBJECTID 6765; approximate area, not the exact launch. Why not exact: imagery verdict 'flag': Pin roughly 40-150 m from the water in woods, a campground or a parking area; launch spot not identifiable at the pin. Coordinate kept only as an area centre.
putInAccess.directions: Starting from East Gate and floating down the river you can do a nice short paddle of 3 miles to Crossroads River Access , or a longer trip of 11 miles to Bookers Bend . Starting upriver, and traveling downriver from Slabtown to East Gate you can paddle or boat to Ross Bridge, a 10 mile trip.
